memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Place the ark of the covenant law in it and shield the ark with the curtain. Bring in the table and set out what belongs on it. Then bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.'" - Exod 40:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the order God gives. The ark first, then everything else.

The ark was where God met His people, above the atonement cover. It went in before the table, before the lampstand, before anything designed for daily service.

Presence before function. Meeting before ministry.

We regularly reverse this. We get the work going, the schedule running, the service organised, and somewhere in the middle we hope to find God. Martha was busy with much serving while Mary sat at Jesus' feet, and He said Mary had chosen what was better (Luke 10:41-42).

Notice also that the curtain immediately shielded the ark. God's presence was placed at the centre and simultaneously guarded — near but holy, accessible but not casual.

That balance is easy to lose. Some of us are so aware of God's holiness that we never come close. Others are so casual that awe disappears entirely. The tabernacle held both: God dwelling among them, behind a curtain.

Through Christ the curtain has been torn (Heb 10:19-20), and we come with confidence — but never with a shrug.

Put the ark in first this week. Everything else can be arranged around it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your week begin with God's presence or with your tasks?
2. Have you lost either nearness to God or awe of Him?
3. What would putting "the ark in first" look like practically for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let my life be arranged around Your presence rather than fitting You into what is left. Amen.
